headline: Multi-cohort transcriptomics and machine learning nominate candidate disease genes
label: Integrative Multiomics Target Discovery
summary: Public cohorts, single-cell data and machine-learning selectors now localize candidate biomarkers to specific cell populations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a layered computational pipeline in which public transcriptomic cohorts are filtered through co-expression modules and machine-learning selectors, then localized to cell populations with single-cell RNA-seq. Examples include a five-gene lysophagy module linked to FOLR2+ macrophages in heart failure, a five-transcription-factor panel tied to macrophage infiltration in cerebral ischemic injury, and a CCL4 biomarker in acute myocardial infarction. Other items add proteomic or metabolic layers, including plasma proteomics in abdominal aortic aneurysm, circulating proteomic profiles in sarcoidosis, and metabolite-protein networks in coronary heart disease. Some studies pair computation with experiments, such as the simulated-spaceflight rat liver model, nuclear RSK1 in primary macrophages and humanized mice, and the STING-Ca2+-TGF-β asthma study. What is new is breadth across cardiovascular, neuroinflammatory, renal, pulmonary, and metabolic contexts, with the workflow carrying the contribution more than any single mechanism.
